title: Water — Basic Physical Facts
text: Water is a chemical compound with the formula H2O: each molecule has two hydrogen atoms covalently bonded to one oxygen atom. At standard atmospheric pressure water freezes at 0 degrees Celsius (32 degrees Fahrenheit) and boils at 100 degrees Celsius (212 degrees Fahrenheit). Its density is greatest near 4 degrees Celsius, which is why ice floats. Water has an unusually high specific heat capacity and is often called the universal solvent because it dissolves many ionic and polar substances. The boiling point decreases at higher altitude because atmospheric pressure is lower.
